source_text:
Ἰδὼν οὖν ὁ κεντυρίων τὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων γενομένην φιλονεικίαν, θεὶς αὐτὸν ἐν μέσῳ, ὡς ἔθος αὐτοῖς, ἔκαυσεν.
οὕτως τε ἡμεῖς ὕστερον ἀνελόμενοι τὰ τιμιώτερα λίθων πολυτελῶν καὶ δοκιμώτερα ὑπὲρ χρυσίον ὀστᾶ αὐτοῦ ἀπεθέμεθα, ὅπου καὶ ἀκόλουθον ἦν.
ἔνθα ὡς δυνατὸν ἡμῖν συναγομένοις ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει καὶ χαρᾷ παρέξει ὁ κύριος ἐπιτελεῖν τὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου αὐτοῦ ἡμέραν γενέθλιον, εἴς τε τὴν τῶν προηθληκότων μνήμην καὶ τῶν μελλόντων ἄσκησίν τε καὶ ἑτοιμασίαν.
thought_title: The centurion burns the body; the church buries the bones and plans an annual commemoration
orientation: The church of Smyrna is concluding its account of Polycarp's death, after the Jews and Nicetes tried to prevent the recovery of his body.
pass_a_gloss: So the centurion, having seen the quarrel of the Jews that had arisen, placed him in the middle, as was their custom, and burned him. And so we later, having taken up his bones, more precious than costly stones and more approved than gold, put them away, where also it was fitting. There, as it is possible for us, when we gather in gladness and joy, the Lord will grant to celebrate the birthday of his martyrdom, for the remembrance of those who have already contended and for the training and preparation of those who are to come.

choices.term: τὰ τιμιώτερα λίθων πολυτελῶν καὶ δοκιμώτερα ὑπὲρ χρυσίον ὀστᾶ
choices.english: his bones, more precious than costly stones and more approved than gold
choices.why: Keeps the comparative force of both adjectives and the explicit objects of comparison, preserving the evaluative contrast the author draws between the bones and material wealth.
rejected: his bones, more valuable than precious stones and finer than gold

choices.why: The verb means to deposit or lay aside for safekeeping; 'put away' keeps the sense of deliberate burial without importing later relic-veneration language.

choices.term: τὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου αὐτοῦ ἡμέραν γενέθλιον
choices.why: The glossary fixes 'birthday' for γενέθλιος ἡμέρα, and the genitive chain must stay literal: the day is the birthday of his martyrdom, not his own birthday.

choices.english: of those who have already contended
choices.why: The perfect participle of προαθλέω refers to those who have already undergone the contest of martyrdom; 'contended' keeps the athletic metaphor without adding 'martyr' explicitly.
rejected: of those who have already been martyred

choices.why: Both nouns are kept as distinct: ἄσκησις is practice or training, ἑτοιμασία is readiness or preparation; the pair is not a hendiadys.

bible_refs.note: τὰ τιμιώτερα λίθων πολυτελῶν καὶ δοκιμώτερα ὑπὲρ χρυσίον echoes Psalm 19:10 (LXX 18:11): 'more to be desired than gold, even much fine gold' and 'sweeter also than honey'.

pass_b_english: When the centurion saw the quarrel the Jews were making, he placed the body in the middle, as was their custom, and burned it.
So afterward we took up his bones, which are more precious than costly stones and more approved than gold, and we put them away where it was fitting.

There, whenever we can gather in gladness and joy, the Lord will grant us to celebrate the birthday of his martyrdom, for the remembrance of those who have already contended and for the training and preparation of those who will.

last_rejected.why: The source says 'burned' (him/it), but the body was already burned in the fire; this refers to cremation after the fire failed. 'Burned it' misrepresents the action.
last_rejected.ruling: ἔκαυσεν means 'burned'; English 'burned it' correctly renders it. Claim about fire context is interpretation, not translation error.

polish.changed: Clarified the centurion as the subject of the first sentence, made the pronoun 'we' explicit in the second sentence, and smoothed the final sentence's rhythm while preserving every claim and qualification.
